recent_articles.title: Over 300 tourists stranded in Gulmarg’s high-altitude cable cars rescued - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Over 320 tourists were rescued from suspended cabins on the **Asia’s highest cable car** in Gulmarg, Kashmir after a technical malfunction. The incident occurred on Monday afternoon when a cable car developed a snag, leaving the cabins dangling mid-air.  The rescue operation lasted over six hours and involved multiple teams of the **State Disaster Response Force (SDRF)**, the **Indian Army**, and additional ATVs from the Gulmarg ATV Association. **J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah** and **Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha** monitored the situation and assured the public that all tourists are safe. The cable car is expected to remain closed for maintenance on May 26th and 27th, with ticket refunds issued for those dates.

recent_articles.title: Disambiguating a year of flux: expert panels at The Hindu Huddle, 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The sixth edition of The Hindu Group's ideas conclave, The Hindu Huddle, will be held in Bengaluru on June 5 and 6, 2026.  **Siddaramaiah**, **D.K. Shivakumar**, and other Chief Ministers from across the country will participate alongside Union Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship **Jayant Chaudhary**, **Omar Abdullah**, **A. Revanth Reddy**, and **K.G. Arunraj**. The event will feature discussions on topics such as tariffs' impact on the Indian economy, diplomacy in managing crises, and artificial intelligence's influence on various aspects of life.  **The Hindu Huddle** is presented by the Sami-Sabinsa Group and co-powered by the Government of Telangana.

recent_articles.title: Kashmir MLA ‘boycotts’ L-G’s drug campaign after demolition drive in his constituency - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sheikh Khursheed**, an MLA from north Kashmir, boycotted a campaign led by **Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha** after the police demolished a house in Langate.  Khursheed criticized the demolition as arbitrary and violating Supreme Court directives, arguing it targeted innocent families based on past accusations. He also questioned the government's focus on drug eradication while ignoring other issues like liquor ban. The **LG Sinha**, meanwhile, launched a campaign to curb drug use in the region, highlighting its connection with terrorism.  The police conducted a demolition drive targeting properties linked to alleged drug traffickers.

recent_articles.title: Jammu and Kashmir leaders ask Omar Abdullah government to follow steps of Tamil Nadu CM Vijay on liquor ban - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dr. Farooq Abdullah**, president of the **National Conference**, stated that a complete ban on liquor sales in **Jammu and Kashmir** is not feasible due to revenue loss concerns, while opposition parties like the **Peoples Democratic Party (PDP)** and **J&K Apni Party** urged the government to follow Tamil Nadu's example by closing down liquor shops.  **Mirwaiz Umar Farooq**, the Kashmir chief cleric, argued that alcohol consumption is socially and religiously discouraged in the region and called for a complete ban on liquor sales to combat drug networks and societal harm.

recent_articles.title: Ever since Elon Musk took over, banning social media accounts became common: Iltija Mufti - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Iltija Mufti**, daughter of former Chief Minister Mehbooba Mufti, is considering legal action against **Meta** for withholding her Twitter and Facebook accounts.  She claims she was not notified before the accounts were suspended and has been unable to contact **Meta**.  Ms. Mufti believes this is part of a pattern of silencing voices critical of the government in Kashmir. She argues that banning political social media accounts is an attack on democracy.

recent_articles.title: J&K CM Abdullah retracts statement on liquor in face of growing criticism - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Omar Abdullah**, the Chief Minister of **Jammu and Kashmir**, retracted his earlier statement that "No one was forcing anyone to consume liquor" after facing criticism.  The **National Conference (NC)** MP, Aga Syed Ruhullah, joined the opposition **Peoples Democratic Party (PDP)** in calling for a ban on all liquor outlets in the state. The PDP leader Iltija Mufti accused the NC of changing its stance and argued that no religion supports alcohol consumption. The BJP stated that legislation alone cannot stop alcohol consumption and emphasized the need for awareness campaigns.

recent_articles.title: Ministers, ambassadors, artists to join The Hindu’s Huddle in June - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Hindu Group** is hosting its annual **The Hindu Huddle**, a conference focused on global issues, in Bengaluru from June 5th to 6th. This year's theme, "A World in Transition," will feature discussions on topics such as regional parties in Indian democracy, diplomacy and conflict resolution, women's representation in Parliament, the role of AI, mental health, and the future of work.  The event will include prominent speakers from India and around the world, including Union Ministers Hardeep Puri and Nitin Gadkari, former President Mohamed Nasheed, and Chinese Ambassador Xu Feihong.

recent_articles.title: Ally Cong. seeks ‘better coordination over crucial public issues’ with ruling NC - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders in **J&K** have called for improved coordination between the party and the **National Conference (NC)**, emphasizing the importance of mutual understanding and cooperation for effective governance.  Following disagreements over Statehood restoration, **Ghulam Ahmad Mir**, a senior Congress leader, stated that concerns and aspirations of the party must be respected to ensure the coalition's continued relevance. This comes after **Dr. Farooq Abdullah**, president of the **NC**, accused the Congress of not doing enough to restore Statehood.

recent_articles.title: NC, PDP in war of words over Rajya Sabha polls, closure of seminary, ‘sidelining’ Urdu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Omar Abdullah**, **J&K Chief Minister**, inaugurated a sports complex in Tangmarg, while **Mehbooba Mufti**, PDP president, criticized the NC for using the Rajya Sabha election results and the closure of the Siraj-ul-Aloom school as political tools. The NC accused the PDP of not appointing polling agents during the Rajya Sabha elections, while the PDP claimed the NC was diverting attention from substantive concerns like the Urdu language erasure and the Waqf Bill.

recent_articles.title: Modi’s party poised for big wins in Indian state elections | Elections News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Narendra Modi’s** Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is expected to win two of four crucial state elections in India, strengthening its position and weakening key rival **Mamata Banerjee**.  The BJP's lead in West Bengal and Assam suggests a significant boost for Modi as he seeks to tackle economic challenges. Opposition parties like the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and All India Trinamool Congress (TMC) are facing setbacks, potentially weakening their opposition against Modi in future elections. The results of these state elections will have long-lasting implications for Indian politics, with analysts predicting a significant shift in power dynamics.

recent_articles.title: Srinagar again ‘full-fledge capital’ of J&K after hiatus of six years - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Srinagar** functioned as the full-fledged summer capital of **Jammu and Kashmir** on Monday, May 4, 2026, after a six-year hiatus.  **Chief Minister Omar Abdullah** received a ceremonial guard of honor at the Civil Secretariat, marking the resumption of the annual Darbar Move tradition. The move, abolished in 2020 by **Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha**, sees over 151 government departments shift offices between Jammu and Srinagar. To accommodate employees, the J&K government inaugurated 368 residential units for them at Sempora, Pampore.

recent_articles.title: BJP closing seminaries with the help of J&K government: Mehbooba Mufti - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mehbooba Mufti**, former **Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir**, criticized the **Omar Abdullah government** for its actions against religious institutions and Urdu language. She accused the government of silencing the closure of educational institutes like Siraj-ul-Uloom in Shopian, which provided education to underprivileged children, and Hazratbal seminary, both allegedly targeted by the BJP. Mufti also stated that the removal of Urdu from revenue department job qualifications represents an attack on Kashmir's identity and culture.

recent_articles.title: No move to drop Urdu from J&K’s revenue services: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Omar Abdullah**, Chief Minister of **Jammu and Kashmir**, denied any plans to drop Urdu from the revenue services, despite opposition parties' claims. He accused the **Peoples Democratic Party (PDP)** of using the language issue as a distraction tactic.  **Sakina Itoo**, a senior J&K minister, stated that Urdu is an essential part of the territory's identity and cannot be removed. The controversy arose after the PDP alleged that Urdu was dropped as a mandatory subject for revenue services recruitment, prompting protests.

recent_articles.title: Railways Minister flags off first Jammu-Srinagar direct train service on ‘historic day’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Union Minister for Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw** and **J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah** celebrated the launch of the first direct train service between Jammu city and Srinagar city.  Vaishnaw described the service as a "gamechanger" for the region's economy, highlighting its impact on cargo movement and tourism. The new rail line connects the Kashmir division with the Jammu division, offering seamless travel to pilgrimage destinations like Shree Mata Vaishno Devi and Shri Amarnath temple. **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** is credited with realizing the dream of railway connectivity in the Kashmir Valley.

recent_articles.title: J&K court orders release of AAP MLA after 8 months of jail, says ‘PSA appears an unjustified exercise’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Jammu and Kashmir High Court** ruled that the detention of **Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) legislator Mehraj Din Malik**, who was arrested for "inappropriate remarks" against a district commissioner, was unjustified. The court deemed the invocation of the Public Safety Act as a shortcut to bypass ordinary criminal law and ordered his release from jail.  The ruling was welcomed by several political parties in the region, including the **J&K Apni Party** and the **J&K Awami Ittehad Party**.

recent_articles.title: J&K CM Omar Abdullah pitches Kashmir as ideal shooting destination to South Indian filmmakers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Omar Abdullah**, the Chief Minister of **Jammu and Kashmir**,  promised to create a welcoming environment for filmmakers during an interaction with South Indian filmmakers in Bengaluru. He emphasized the state's scenic beauty and cultural heritage as attractive features for film production, stating his government will extend full support to make filmmaking easier and more accessible.

recent_articles.title: Election Commission, and not the BJP, seems to be fighting Trinamool in West Bengal, says Kapil Sibal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kapil Sibal**, a senior Supreme Court lawyer and Rajya Sabha MP, criticized the **Election Commission of India (ECI)**'s actions in West Bengal ahead of the upcoming elections. He accused the **EC** and the **BJP** of working together to suppress the Trinamool Congress (TMC), alleging an "unconstitutional Emergency" and a disproportionate deployment of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF).  Other opposition leaders, including **Arvind Kejriwal**, have also expressed concern over the situation.

recent_articles.title: MP Rashid’s party moves bail application to attend ailing father in Srinagar; NC’s Farooq Abdullah demands release - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Awami Ittehad Party (AIP)** filed an interim bail application for jailed party chief Engineer Rashid to visit his critically ill father in Srinagar.  **Dr. Farooq Abdullah**, president of the **National Conference (NC)**, also demanded Rashid's release, emphasizing the humanitarian aspect of the situation. Several legislators and leaders from various parties visited the hospital where Rashid's father is being treated.
